verified_premises: Cloud seeding and other local weather-modification projects exist and are reportable activities in the United States.
The WMO describes weather modification as local-to-regional intervention and says it cannot create whole weather systems or eliminate severe weather phenomena.
packets.unsupported_inference: The existence of cloud seeding does not establish that it caused a particular flood, storm, or other disaster, much less that the event was covertly engineered.
unknowns: The effect size of a particular documented project depends on meteorological conditions and study design.

unknowns: Specific enforcement powers and transport rules must be checked in the actual local proposal.

verified_premises: Coordinated networks, automated accounts, paid commenters, and AI-assisted influence campaigns exist.

unknowns: Account automation and common control require platform or network evidence, not writing-style intuition alone.

verified_premises: Google Trends uses a sample of searches and reports normalized relative interest rather than a complete count or log of individual queries.
Low-volume terms, geographic filters, time zones, sampling variation, and later recalculation can make screenshots unstable or easy to overinterpret.
A 2026 fact-check documented claims that apparent pre-event searches proved a public attack was staged.
packets.unsupported_inference: An apparent pre-event spike or later-changing Trends graph does not by itself prove foreknowledge, identify a planner, or establish that an attack was staged.
unknowns: A specific screenshot may require its original URL, query syntax, collection time, time zone, comparison terms, raw scale, repeated samples, and evidence of alteration before it can be interpreted.

unknowns: Each component claim needs its own dated evidence chain; confidence cannot be transferred between unrelated claims.
